claim: AWS Config provides a detailed view of the configuration of AWS resources in your account, including how resources are related to one another and how they were configured in the past, so you can see how configurations and relationships change over time.
question: What is AWS Config, in one sentence?

values.display: how the resources are related to one another
how they were configured in the past
how the configurations and relationships change over time

evidence.quote: AWS Config provides a detailed view of the configuration of AWS resources in your AWS account. This includes how the resources are related to one another and how they were configured in the past so that you can see how the configurations and relationships change over time.

claim: AWS Config rules evaluate the configuration settings of your resources; when a resource violates a rule's conditions, AWS Config flags it as noncompliant and sends a notification, evaluating resources continuously as they are created, changed or deleted.
question: What happens when a resource breaks an AWS Config rule?

values.display: flags the resource as noncompliant and sends a notification
continuously evaluates your resources as they are created, changed, or deleted

evidence.quote: When AWS Config detects that a resource violates the conditions in one of your rules, AWS Config flags the resource as noncompliant and sends a notification. AWS Config continuously evaluates your resources as they are created, changed, or deleted.

claim: With AWS Config you can view the IAM policy assigned to a user, group or role at any time Config was recording, and the security group port rules that were open at a specific time.
question: How can you find which security group rules were open on a past date?

values.display: view the IAM policy that was assigned to a user, group, or role
the port rules that were open at a specific time

evidence.quote: You can also use AWS Config to view the configuration of your EC2 security groups, including the port rules that were open at a specific time.
You can use AWS Config to view the IAM policy that was assigned to a user, group, or role at any time in which AWS Config was recording.

claim: By default, AWS Config creates configuration items for every supported resource in the Region; you can instead specify the resource types it records.
question: Which resources does AWS Config record by default?

values.display: creates configuration items for every supported resource in the region
specify the resource types that you want it to track

evidence.quote: By default, AWS Config creates configuration items for every supported resource in the region. If you don't want AWS Config to create configuration items for all supported resources, you can specify the resource types that you want it to track.

claim: AWS Config supports continuous recording, which records configuration changes whenever they occur, and daily recording, which gives a configuration item with the most recent state over the last 24-hour period only if it differs from the previous one.
question: What is the difference between AWS Config continuous and daily recording?

values.display: record configuration changes continuously whenever a change occurs
the most recent state of your resources over the last 24-hour period
values.spoken: the most recent state over the last twenty-four hours

evidence.quote: AWS Config supports *Continuous recording* and *Daily recording*. Continuous recording allows you to record configuration changes continuously whenever a change occurs. Daily recording allows you to receive a configuration item (CI) representing the most recent state of your resources over the last 24-hour period, only if it’s different from the previous CI recorded.

note: d085. The launch date of daily recording belongs to the numbers+changes lens.

claim: A configuration item is a point-in-time view of the attributes of a supported AWS resource (metadata, attributes, relationships, current configuration and related events); AWS Config creates one whenever it detects a change to a resource type it records.
question: What is an AWS Config configuration item?

values.display: a point-in-time view of the various attributes
whenever it detects a change to a resource type that it is recording

evidence.quote: A *configuration item* represents a point-in-time view of the various attributes of a supported AWS resource that exists in your account. The components of a configuration item include metadata, attributes, relationships, current configuration, and related events. AWS Config creates a configuration item whenever it detects a change to a resource type that it is recording.

question: What does the AWS Config configuration recorder do, and what kinds are there?

AWS Config uses the Amazon SNS topic that you specify to send you notifications.
doesn't modify the lifecycle policies

evidence.quote: AWS Config tracks changes in the configuration of your AWS resources, and it regularly sends updated configuration details to an Amazon S3 bucket that you specify.
AWS Config uses the Amazon SNS topic that you specify to send you notifications.
AWS Config only delivers the configuration history files and configuration snapshots to the specified S3 bucket; AWS Config doesn't modify the lifecycle policies for objects in the S3 bucket.

Lambda functions
Guard

evidence.quote: | Managed rules | Predefined, customizable rules created by AWS Config. | For a list of managed rules, see [List of AWS Config Managed Rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/managed-rules-by-aws-config.html). |

claim: AWS Config rule triggers are configuration changes (evaluate when an in-scope resource changes), periodic (evaluate at a frequency you choose) or hybrid (both).
question: When does an AWS Config rule run?

values.display: there is a change in configuration of the resource
at a frequency that you choose
Some rules have both configuration change and periodic triggers.

evidence.quote: | Periodic | AWS Config runs evaluations for the rule at a frequency that you choose; for example, every 24 hours. |

| Hybrid | Some rules have both configuration change and periodic triggers. For these rules, AWS Config evaluates your resources when it detects a configuration change and also at the frequency that you specify.  |
Depending on the rule, AWS Config will evaluate your resources either in response to configuration changes or periodically.

note: d086. Display 'there is a change in configuration of the resource' is in the Configuration changes row (long row, not quoted); kept only if M7 holds it via the claim.

claim: AWS Config rules have two evaluation modes: proactive evaluates resources before they are deployed, and detective evaluates resources that are already deployed; proactive rules do not remediate noncompliant resources or prevent them from being deployed.
question: Does an AWS Config proactive rule block a noncompliant deployment?

values.display: evaluate resources before they have been deployed
evaluate resources that have already been deployed
Proactive rules do not remediate resources

evidence.quote: | Detective | Use detective evaluation to evaluate resources that have already been deployed. This allows you to evaluate the configuration settings of your existing resources. |
Proactive rules do not remediate resources that are flagged as NON\_COMPLIANT or prevent them from being deployed.

claim: A conformance pack is a collection of AWS Config rules and remediation actions deployed as a single entity in an account and Region or across an organization; you author it as a YAML template or start from a sample template.
question: How do you deploy a set of Config rules and remediations, for example for PCI DSS, as one unit across an organization?

values.display: a collection of AWS Config rules and remediation actions
deployed as a single entity
authoring a YAML template

qualifiers.scope: per account and Region, or per organization

evidence.quote: A conformance pack is a collection of AWS Config rules and remediation actions that can be easily deployed as a single entity in an account and a Region or across an organization in AWS Organizations.
Conformance packs are created by authoring a YAML template that contains the list of AWS Config managed or custom rules and remediation actions.

claim: An AWS Config aggregator collects configuration and compliance data from multiple source accounts and Regions into one account at no additional cost, but it is a read-only view: you cannot deploy rules or push snapshot files to source accounts through it.
question: Can you deploy Config rules to member accounts through an aggregator?

values.display: collects AWS Config configuration and compliance data from multiple source accounts and regions
Aggregators provide a *read-only view*
Using aggregators does not incur any additional costs.
you cannot deploy rules through an aggregator

evidence.quote: An aggregator collects AWS Config configuration and compliance data from multiple source accounts and regions.

Aggregators provide a *read-only view* into the source accounts and regions that the aggregator is authorized to view by replicating data from the source accounts into the aggregator account. Aggregators do not provide mutating access into a source account or region. For example, this means that you cannot deploy rules through an aggregator or push snapshot files to a source account or region through an aggregator.
Using aggregators does not incur any additional costs.

claim: An aggregator's source accounts can be individual accounts or an organization in AWS Organizations; you provide them individually or retrieve them through AWS Organizations.
question: Must you use AWS Organizations to create an AWS Config aggregator?

values.display: can be an individual account or an organization in AWS Organizations

evidence.quote: A source account can be an individual account or an organization in AWS Organizations. You can provide source accounts individually or you can retrieve them through AWS Organizations.

claim: AWS Config tracks resource changes by calling Describe or List APIs, and it also tracks configuration changes not initiated by an API by examining resource configurations periodically.
question: Does AWS Config catch configuration changes that were not made through an API call?

values.display: invoking the Describe or the List API call
tracks the configuration changes that were not initiated by the API

evidence.quote: AWS Config keeps track of all changes to your resources by invoking the Describe or the List API call for each resource in your account.

AWS Config also tracks the configuration changes that were not initiated by the API. AWS Config examines the resource configurations periodically and generates configuration items for the configurations that have changed.
